subject: Renewal: Contract restructure & capacity growth
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: tom.reyes@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T10:15:00Z
Subject: Renewal: Contract restructure & capacity growth

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well — we’re starting to plan our contract renewal window (Aug 1) and want to explore shifting the structure for the next term. A few things on our side:

- We expect a 2.5x increase in inference usage across our federated apps over the next 12 months (most growth H2).
- Leadership prefers a multi-year commitment if we can get predictable pricing + a staged ramp rather than a big up-front bucket.
- We need better co-term handling across three subsidiaries (US / CA / EU) and a simple auto-renew opt-out process for acquisitions.

Questions for you: do you have a standard 2-year staged ramp structure? Can Redwood support quarterly true-ups and burst capacity without long provisioning lead time? Also, can you share an initial commercial term sheet we can review with procurement?

Cc’ing Tom (ops) who will own the capacity activation calendar.

Thanks,
Aisha
Procurement Lead
Nimbus Health

[Attachment: usage_history_export_Mar-May2026.csv (CSV — summary of current month usage by product)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-21T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: Contract restructure & capacity growth

Aisha — thanks for the clear context and the usage export, that’s helpful. High-level response and three options for your leadership to consider: 

1) Two-year staged-commit (recommended)
   - Year 1: baseline commit = current run-rate x1.25 with quarterly staged increases (Q1 +10%, Q2 +30%, Q3 +40%)
   - Year 2: baseline increases by 25% on anniversary with an option to convert unused committed tokens to credits for burst consumption
   - Pricing: 8% discount vs annual renewals; SLOs and dedicated capacity window for scheduled bursts

2) Annual with ramp credits (low friction)
   - One-year term with pre-paid credits and monthly true-ups; more flexibility but higher unit price

3) Enterprise co-term (across subsidiaries) + shared pool
   - Single master agreement + regional SOWs; shared burst pool and central governance for auto-renew opt-outs (triggered by M&A events)

We can support quarterly true-ups and on-demand burst for the volumes you’re describing; burst provisioning for reserved capacity uses our dedicated pool with a 24–72 hour activation SLA depending on GPU class.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick call to confirm which option aligns with procurement/finance, 2) I’ll circulate a one-page commercial term sheet and a short ops playbook (activation-runbook + onramp calendar).

I’ve looped in Marissa (Customer Success) to confirm onboarding credits and migration runway; Karhtik (AE) will own commercial terms and discounting. Available for 30-min call Wed/Thu.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Tel: +1 415 555 0112

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nimbushealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-22T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: Contract restructure & capacity growth

Aisha / Grace — quick note from ops/CS perspective:

- For a staged two-year ramp we typically include 120 days of accelerated onboarding credits to offset the earlier higher consumption during model rollouts. I recommend a 3-month credit tranche unlocked at each quarter milestone.
- Activation plan: we’ll split the first 90 days into pilot (non-prod) -> canary (limited prod) -> full activation. Each region will have a capacity plan; for EU subsidiaries we’ll reserve a separate GPU pool to avoid cross-region latency impact.
- Metrics: require a 30-day ramp review at each milestone (usage, latency, cost per token) with automatic rollback to fallback model variant if regressions detected.

I’ll attach the ops playbook and a sample onboarding schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops_playbook_staged_onboarding.pdf (PDF — activation runbook)]

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbushealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: Contract restructure & capacity growth

Grace / Marissa — thanks for the options. Leadership is leaning to option #1 (2-year staged-commit) but we have two asks before we can sign: 

1) A clear top-up / true-up cadence that avoids double-billing during transition months — we want quarterly reconciliations tied to usage windows.
2) A flexible burst allowance: ability to add up to 50% temporary capacity for up to 30 days with billing only for actual consumed tokens and an agreed max per month to cap runaway costs.

If you can put a short amendment together with those specifics we can expedite with procurement. Also please include the SLOs for activation time when we request burst capacity.

Tom
Director, Cloud Ops
Nimbus Health

Tom / Aisha — appreciate the direction. Attached is a first-pass one-page amendment (term_amendment_v1.pdf) that includes:

- 2-year staged-commit with the quarterly increase ladder you described
- Quarterly reconciliation windows (invoiced adjustments applied to next invoice; credits applied where appropriate)
- Burst allowance: up to 50% temporary capacity for up to 30 days with consumption billing; activation SLA: 24–72 hours depending on GPU class; cap mechanism enforced by per-month cap and an emergency escalation path
- Co-terming language: master agreement + regional SOWs; acquisitions clause that allows a 90-day auto-renew opt-out notice

Karthik — please review the commercial terms (esp. discounting and credit conversion language) and suggest edits. Marissa — the ops playbook PDF is in your earlier note; please confirm the 90/30 pilot -> canary -> full activation cadence and the 30-day ramp-review checkpoints and I will bake that into v1.

If this aligns, I’ll create a DocuSign envelope for procurement and a HubSpot deal update (RDW-2391) with expected signature date of 2026-06-10.
